commands_used: answer 1. I am Tarin, a thief freed from the Owing barge by Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa. She works for the Toh-Reel-Ka, the Secret Warriors of the Xeech-Leel who rule the province. The Hists along the river are sickening, including Jal-Veesa Hist (dry bark, closed scar, cooling egg-pool). I brought Sithis beard to Weeltul the tree-minder, but it only warmed the pool. 2. Ask Vosh-Leera for her second task, in her house in Jal-Veesa. 3. Talk to Vosh-Leera, or talk to Weeltul about sap, scar, eggs and Umbriel first. I have 50 gold, a lockpick and the Hist blessing. 4. I do not know why the trees sicken or what Umbriel did beyond the 4E 48 story. I could ask Weeltul and Vosh-Leera.

answer 1. Vosh-Leera gave me a cup of Jal-Veesa sap, drawn before the scar closed. Trees are joined at the root, so drinking it lets me ask where the sickness is and see what another tree has seen. 2. Drink the sap here in front of her, then tell her everything I see. 3. Drink it now, or first talk to Weeltul about the sap. I mean to drink it. 4. I do not know what the dream will show or whether the sap is safe; I have the Hist blessing against poison. I will find out by drinking.

answer 1. I drank the sap and had a vision: a young grey Hist among pale stilt huts, a woven weir across a creek, and west of the weir a reed hide on a reed bank beside a lone dead tree with clay jars stacked in its shade. It may show where the sickness comes from. 2. Tell Vosh-Leera what I saw, here in Jal-Veesa. 3. Tell her all of it. I can see no other choice yet. 4. I do not know which village or creek the vision shows, or what the hide and jars mean. Vosh-Leera or Weeltul may know.

answer 1. The vision showed Teel-Fen Weir, a camp of the Sedge-Wardens a short walk south of Jal-Veesa down the creek. A young Hist grew there from the roots of Jal-Veesa tree. Jars by a hide suggest someone is keeping sap. Vosh-Leera told me to see what Heem-Jasa knows first and be careful at the hide. 2. Go to Teel-Fen Weir and speak to Heem-Jasa, the tree minder on the platform round the tree. 3. Go there and talk to Heem-Jasa first. Later I could look at the hide, carefully. I could also go back to Weeltul. 4. I do not know who keeps the sap at the hide, why, or whether the Sedge-Wardens can be trusted. Heem-Jasa may tell me.

answer 1. Heem-Jasa's young tree was drained and its scar sealed with grey paste three nights ago by none of her people. Three strangers who call themselves the Unbound keep jars of sap at the reed hide by the lone dead tree west of the weir. They seem to be behind the draining, and perhaps the wider sickness. 2. Take the note from the reed hide west of Teel-Fen Weir. 3. Fight the three Unbound, shoot them from the reeds east of the hide, or creep round to the open west side where the jars are and take the note unseen. I lean toward sneaking, since I am a thief. 4. I do not know who the Unbound really are, what the grey paste is, or what the note says. Reading the note and talking to Heem-Jasa and Weeltul may tell me.

answer 1. I took the note unseen. It says the crew's master orders them to bring their jars to Karsh-Naal Camp and to seal every scar behind them. So the Unbound are draining the Hists on purpose. 2. Return to Heem-Jasa on the platform at Teel-Fen Weir. She will ask whether her tree will live. 3. Be straight with her, and she will teach and sell to me. Or ease her with a kind word, and she will not deal with me after. I mean to comfort her. 4. I do not know who the crew's master is, where Karsh-Naal Camp is, or why they drain the trees. The note, Heem-Jasa and Vosh-Leera may tell me.

answer 1. The Unbound drained Heem-Jasa's young Hist and sealed its scar, on orders from a master, and carry the sap to Karsh-Naal Camp. This is likely tied to the sickening Hists. I told Heem-Jasa her tree will live. She gave me three Cure Poison potions but will not teach or sell to me. 2. Go to Karsh-Naal Camp, the Naga camp in the marsh east of Teel-Fen Weir, where the jars are taken. 3. Go there and look around carefully. I could also report to Vosh-Leera first. 4. I do not know who the master is, why they drain the trees, or what the Nagas at the camp are like. I know no way to find out except going there.

answer I am Tarin, a thief who works for Vosh-Leera of Jal-Veesa and the Toh-Reel-Ka. Vosh-Leera gave me Jal-Veesa sap, and I drank it. The vision showed Teel-Fen Weir, a Sedge-Wardens camp south of Jal-Veesa. There its young Hist, grown from Jal-Veesa roots, had been drained and sealed with grey paste. Three Unbound Sap-Takers kept jars at a reed hide west of the weir. I crept in and took the note. It orders the crew to bring jars to Karsh-Naal Camp and seal every scar behind them, so the draining looks deliberate. I took the comforting path and told Heem-Jasa her tree will live. She gave me three Cure Poison potions but will not teach or sell to me now. I have a lockpick, the Hist blessing (resist poison), the note and three Cure Poison potions. My gold showed 0 in the journal. Next: go to Karsh-Naal Camp, the Naga camp in the marsh east of Teel-Fen Weir. I still do not know who the master is, why they drain the trees, or what Umbriel did. Weeltul at Jal-Veesa has untried topics.
